correctness.rationale: For binary vertices, distance differences are the dot product of a landmark sign row with the vertex difference, and every ternary displacement occurs. If the rows have rank at most three, complete them, if needed, to a span generated by three independent sign rows. A nonzero cofactor null vector of these three rows has entries in {0,±4}, since any 3-by-3 sign determinant is divisible by 4 and has absolute value at most 3√3. Dividing by 4 gives a nonzero ternary null vector for the original rows. Thus no smaller landmark set resolves, and for four landmarks nonsingularity is necessary and sufficient. A fresh exhaustive enumeration using pair separation (not the sign test) considered every subset of size 0–4, generated legal slides to unoccupied Hamming neighbors and computed breadth-first distances from every basis. It reproduced 928 vertices, 3584 edges, one component, degree counts 7:512, 8:384, 16:32, and eccentricity counts 8:64, 9:592, 10:272. The radius and diameter are 8 and 10. Coordinate permutations and translations act by slide-graph isometries, and canonicalization under these actions reproduced all eight representatives and their orbit sizes, degrees and eccentricities exactly, including the two degree-16 populations of size 16 with eccentricities 9 and 10.
residual_risks: The orbits are under the natural hypercube isometries, not a claim about the full automorphism group of the relocation graph. The exhaustion proves only the four-dimensional assertion.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the exact ordinary-metric-basis, adjacency-restricted slide graph of Q4, in particular its distance invariants and orbit-resolved eccentricities. The minimum size and general ternary-kernel method are known. The strongest indexed comparisons either change the dimension, change the resolving condition and allow unrestricted exchanges, or change the host. Published static symmetry work could overlap the underlying basis-orbit classification; the available abstract does not settle that question. No priority credit for the static orbit count alone is needed for the slide-graph claim.
residual_risks: Whether Nikolić–Čangalović–Grujičić classifies ordinary Q4 bases or their static orbits remains unresolved. The Beardon full text was also unavailable.
One focused literature lookup did not find a directly matching slide theorem. That does not rule out earlier reconfiguration work under another term.

value.rationale: Requiring a single hypercube-edge move is a natural geometric restriction on matroid exchanges. It makes reachability and shortest legal sequences separate questions from static metric dimension. The exact radius and diameter give sharp best-center and worst-case move counts; the eight-orbit census explains why even maximum-degree bases need not have the same farthest distance. These are useful exact low-dimensional benchmarks, not only a count of bases or an arbitrary parameter substitution.
residual_risks: The proof is finite exhaustive computation for the natural Q4 case. It gives neither a general Q_d slide-distance theorem nor a classification of all automorphisms of the slide graph.
